title: Doenjang Jjigae
subtitle: Korean fermented soybean paste stew with tofu and vegetables
excerpt: Doenjang jjigae is the Korean equivalent of comfort in a bowl. The fermented soybean paste gives the broth a deep, savoury flavour. It is made with tofu, courgette, and mushrooms, and is on the table in 30 minutes. It is one of the most common dishes in Korean home cooking.
sourceNotes: Doenjang jjigae is one of the most traditional Korean stews. Doenjang (fermented soybean paste) has been produced in Korea for over a thousand years. The stew is considered a staple of Korean home cooking and is eaten at virtually every meal. It is similar in concept to Japanese miso soup but richer and more substantial.

content.text: Doenjang jjigae is built around the deep, savoury flavour of fermented soybean paste. It takes about 30 minutes from start to finish and fills the kitchen with a warm, inviting smell. The tofu should be firm enough to hold its shape in the stew -- handle it gently so it does not break up too much.

items.prepNote: use 300g firm tofu -- cut into 2cm cubes
use dashima or anchovy stock for a more traditional flavour
use 3 tbsp doenjang Korean soybean paste -- dissolve in a spoonful of hot stock before adding

content.text: Bring the stock to a simmer in a medium saucepan. Add the garlic.
Dissolve the doenjang paste in a ladleful of hot stock, then stir back into the pan.
Add the courgette and mushrooms. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the tofu cubes. Simmer gently for 5 more minutes. Do not stir vigorously.
Taste and add salt or more doenjang if needed. Add chilli flakes if using.
Scatter spring onion over the top. Serve with steamed rice and kimchi on the side.

items.symptom: Stew tastes flat despite adding enough doenjang
items.cause: Doenjang not fully dissolved or stock too weak
items.fix: Always dissolve doenjang separately in hot stock before adding to the pot. If the broth is thin, add a little more doenjang -- the flavour should be deep and savoury, not mild.

content.text: Doenjang jjigae is Korean soul food. It is served at nearly every home meal. The fermented paste gives the broth a complexity that no other ingredient can replicate. In Korea, each family has its own balance of vegetables and protein. This version is a good starting point.
